mechanism_narrative: Transit mobility has been recovering from -31.1 to -30.0 over three weeks, signaling increased out-of-home activity that precedes higher retail footfall. RETAIL_REC will rise over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -31.1 at t-3w to -30.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28-day mean of -11.3 despite TRANSIT remaining above -31.1.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility below -20 indicates adverse conditions that reduce overall discretionary trips. When PARKS falls below -20, RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -9.1 at t-1w to -20.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than or equal to the last 14-day mean when PARKS stays below -20.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising WORKPLACES and falling RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a return to office work, which increases weekday retail traffic. When WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls simultaneously, RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases while RESIDENTIAL decreases week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -8.6 to -8.0 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 3.9 to 3.6 between t-3w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28-day mean when WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: During a reopening regime characterized by TRANSIT recovery above -30, retail mobility responds positively to transit gains. As TRANSIT crosses above -30, RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has been above -30 for three of four weeks, reaching -28.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than the last 14-day mean when TRANSIT is above -30.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility near zero indicates essential trips are stable. A rise above zero signals reduced stockpiling and more discretionary retail. When GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 0, RETAIL_REC increases over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 0.7 at t-1w and -0.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than the last 7-day mean when GROCERY_PHARM is above 0.

mechanism_narrative: High RESIDENTIAL mobility (stay-at-home) suppresses retail, and when combined with low PARKS (less outdoor socializing), the suppression is stronger. When RESIDENTIAL > 3 and PARKS < -15, RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 3.6 and PARKS was -20.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than the last 14-day mean when RESIDENTIAL > 3 and PARKS < -15.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in WORKPLACES below -8.5 indicates renewed remote work, which reduces weekday retail. When WORKPLACES falls below -8.5, RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES was -8.6 at t-3w and -8.0 at t-0w, hovering near threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28-day mean when WORKPLACES drops below -8.5.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime where TRANSIT is recovering, retail follows transit with a one-week lag. When TRANSIT improves week-on-week, RETAIL_REC rises the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -31.1 to -30.1 then to -28.1, then fell to -30.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than the last 7-day mean in weeks following a week-on-week TRANSIT increase.
